scope: Krea2 (k2) branch: VNCCS pose depth as a selectable control source
problem: The k2 branch already routed a depth map into the Krea2 depth ControlNet-LoRA, but the VNCCS pose studio output (1172) only fed a preview and a before/after compare node, so the pose reference never reached the model.

change.pattern_alignment: same shape as the existing line-art source selector 1157

added_nodes.title: [05B6] Depth 来源选择（参考图 / VNCCS 姿势）

change.branch_and_group: the three nodes are appended to the k2 branch nodeIds and tagged uap_layout_group CORE-05 参考预处理与控制图生成 · K2 Krea2
change.default_behaviour: select=(none) with mode=priority resolves to input_01, so the encoded control and the rendered result stay as they were until the dropdown selects input_02

source_preservation.other_nodes_and_parameters: only the three nodes above were added and one link was rerouted; no existing widget, mode, title or prompt changed
source_preservation.branch_metadata: k2 nodeIds gained the three new ids only
source_preservation.encoding_note: links in this file use the array form [id, origin, origin_slot, target, target_slot, type]

structural.note: subgraph boundary ports (-10 / -20) are excluded by design

depth_source_ab.method: one frontend session, the pose capture pre-uploaded once so both runs use the same pose, then two submissions that differ only in the switch position
depth_source_ab.reading: the encoder output follows whichever depth source the switch selects; the two sources themselves are unchanged between runs

limits: One prompt, one seed and one pose; the comparison isolates the base model and LoRA strength, not sampler variety.
Pose fidelity is judged from rendered images; no landmark or pose-matching metric was computed.
The Turbo base at LoRA strength 4 is a broken configuration, not evidence about control effectiveness.
The probes that replaced node 1191 ran only in the isolated runtime.

deployment.restart: saved original command line with AKI_HUISHI_PROFILE=production

on_off_on.reading: switching the depth control on does not change the render, and the off case reproduces

noise control image.reading: the control path can strongly affect sampling

probes.reading: arbitrary control images all change the render, so the chain is wired and injecting; the natural depth map is the case that lands in the same basin as the unconstrained model

full_sampling.interpretation: Krea2 depth control is wired and can affect sampling, but with this Turbo base model, 8 steps and LoRA strength 1 it is not distinguishable from no control when the control map is the natural depth of the reference image

effectiveness_comparison.question: the full sampling showed control-on and control-off rendering identical pixels with the Turbo base; this comparison asks whether the depth control works at all
effectiveness_comparison.method: fixed prompt, seed, pose capture and workflow; each configuration submitted twice (control off / on) and compared pixel by pixel

configurations.label: DaSiWa Turbo, 8 steps, CFG 1, LoRA strength 1
configurations.reading: the render changes, but the pose does not follow the control map

configurations.label: DaSiWa Turbo, 8 steps, CFG 1, LoRA strength 4
configurations.reading: the Turbo render collapses into noise at strength 4 in both arms, so this setting is unusable rather than informative

configurations.label: Krea2-Anime v2.0 (non-distilled), 24 steps, CFG 3.5, LoRA strength 1
configurations.reading: control-off draws a plain standing figure; control-on reproduces the seated forward-leaning pose from the pose depth, with the pond and flower the control map carries

effectiveness_comparison.conclusion: the Krea2 depth ControlNet-LoRA is effective with the non-distilled Krea2-Anime v2.0 base; the Turbo base is what made the earlier comparison look inert, and LoRA strength 4 breaks the Turbo render entirely
effectiveness_comparison.not_changed: the deployed workflow still has its own base model, strength and sampler settings; the comparison changed them only inside the isolated runtime

changes.before: DaSiWa Krea2 - Turbo - Raw CuteDisaster v2 Turbo UC BF16

live_acceptance.route: real frontend on the deployed workflow, workflow prompt, fixed seed

default_base_switch.user_data_preserved: prompts, seeds, sizes, LoRA stack, control strength and all other branches keep their values

erase_verification.question: does the line-art erase ([05C7] ImageCompositeMasked) actually remove anything

current_state.mask_semantics: LoadImage derives MASK from alpha only; a file without an alpha channel has no transparency, mask = 1 - alpha is all zeros

measured.method: same run settings, [05C2] mask swapped between the referenced file and a hand-made mask with a transparent rectangle, control image [05K-PREVIEW] compared

erase_verification.conclusion: the erase is a no-op with the currently referenced mask file; a mask that really carries transparency changes the control image, so the node chain itself works

pose_follow_verification.method: two VNCCS poses (the stored seated pose, and thighs/calves rotated to raise the legs), same seed, prompt and workflow; pose capture re-uploaded per run so the depth is deterministic
pose_follow_verification.visual: the seated pose renders a crouched figure tending a plant; the raised-legs pose renders a standing figure with both arms held out, matching the control map
pose_follow_verification.limits: responsiveness and pose direction are verified; exact joint-level fidelity is judged from the images, not from a landmark metric, and the prompt names a full-body framing

causes: the erase composite [05C7] had no downstream consumer: its only sink was the preview [05V7], while the control chain read 1191 DepthAnything <- 1153 <- 1190 reference image
the mask loader [05C2] was muted (mode=2), so its MASK output never reached the composite
its image widget pointed at ComfyUI_temp_oflff_00001_.png, an ordinary RGB render without alpha, while properties.image still recorded the editor-saved RGBA mask
fixes: repoint 130160.input_01 from 1191 to 1147 so the erased line art reaches the control image
notes: my earlier reading that unmuting plus swapping the file still changed nothing was an artefact: the test harness unmutes the whole k2 branch during preparation, so the mute variable did not exist in those runs
partial_execution_targets must be strings; integers are rejected with HTTP 400 and leave no history entry
erase_repair.mask_semantics: LoadImage derives MASK from alpha, so transparent areas become mask=1 and are the areas the composite fills with black

erase_subgraph_investigation.goal: make the Krea2 erase segment a subgraph with its own instance per branch
attempts: hand-written definition in the frontend format (structurally identical to the working one, loaded fine after adding inputNode/outputNode bounding, but the instance output never resolved)
frontend-side conversion via app.rootGraph.convertToSubgraph() with correct definitions and wiring (verified byte-for-byte between file and live graph)
erase_subgraph_investigation.measurement: converted in the live page, ran two renders that differ only in the mask file; the control image hash was identical (9eaf73ce), so the subgraph output never reached the encoder
erase_subgraph_investigation.cause: the frontend export cannot resolve a subgraph output into a DazzleSwitch (dynamic/wildcard input): the link exists in the graph and survives reload, but graphToPrompt omits that input and the switch falls back to the next available input
erase_subgraph_investigation.consequence: the Krea2 erase chain stays flat inside the k2 branch; the Anima branches keep their own copy inside the [05] subgraph, so neither branch depends on the other

anima_erase_mask_fix.what: the erase subgraph inside 高级 · 擦线与导出 (used by the Anima branches and by both Anima suites) pointed its mask loader at ComfyUI_temp_oflff_00001_.png, an RGB render without alpha, which made the erase a no-op
anima_erase_mask_fix.fix: image widget set to clipspace/clipspace-painted-masked-1782566128506.png in all six sources: the UAP workflow and template plus both Anima suite workflows and templates
anima_erase_mask_fix.evidence: the minimal chain test showed the RGBA mask changes the composite by 20.17% of pixels while the RGB file changes nothing
